chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Hariz, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave a man money for Hajj to perform Hajj on his behalf from Al-Kufa, but he performed Hajj on his behalf from Al-Basra. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, if he fulfills all its rituals, then his Hajj is complete.'

key_terms.الْبَصْرَةِ: Al-Basra, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Al-Kufa, a major city in Iraq
key_terms.حَجَّةً: Money or funds allocated for performing Hajj
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.مَنَاسِكِهِ: Its rituals (referring to the rites of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Is Hajj valid if performed on behalf of someone else from a different city than specified?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in the geographical stipulations of Hajj on behalf of another (Hajj al-Tamattu' or 'Ifrad), affirming that validity rests on the completion of core rituals rather than strict adherence to the point of departure. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor deviations in logistical details do not invalidate the spiritual obligation, provided the pilgrim fulfills all essential rites. This ruling underscores the practical ease (taysir) intended by the Imams in facilitating religious duties for the community.
